label: Cover
notes: One line: Marshal is the commanding operational authority of the PyForge Dream-to-Code factory — the BMAD-method orchestrator that turns a solidified Dream into validated code without vibe coding. Since 2026-07-31 this is shipped software: Epic 1 landed 10 of 10 stories, six real commands, 785 tests. The supervisor is the product. This deck now carries the whole ecosystem story — the Charter, the Guild, and the operating model — since Marshal absorbed the genesis big picture.

label: Act I — The Commander
notes: Act I: who Marshal is and the problem the factory answers. Eight stations make the Guild and the Charter gives execution exactly one owner. Then the two mindsets that make autonomy safe: anti-vibe pragmatism and ruthless context containment.

label: The problem
notes: Autonomous coding fails two ways: unattended agents ship plausible-but-wrong code, or humans review everything and the speed evaporates. Marshal's answer is structural — deterministic orchestration, spec gates before merge, scope checks on frozen surfaces, independent verification. Gates are never weakened to raise the autonomy share. The receipts: 128 stories shipped fleet-wide, zero frozen-surface violations reaching a merge.

label: Anti-vibe pragmatism
notes: The core mindset: Marshal operates entirely on strict structural inputs. Good intentions and close-enough do not exist. A sub-agent that deviates from the spec is flagged instantly and forced into a corrective iteration.

label: Ruthless context containment
notes: Mindset two: context discipline. Each sub-agent receives only the exact context its task requires. Containment kills hallucination and keeps the line fast.

label: The Dream-to-Code pipeline
notes: The operating model, tier by tier. The Dream is yours — raw aspiration in a markdown file. Herald renders the Pitch. Then the two tiers Marshal owns: the Spec, a five-field machine contract, and the Build, gated story loops. At the top: Realized — shipped and governed, patrolled by deterministic detectors. Every Dream shows at its furthest stage on the live console.

label: Act III — Running the line
notes: Act III: the machinery — one story's journey, the three ways work flows, the autonomy gradient, the staffed SDLC, and the relay that hands work across all eight stations.

label: One story's journey
notes: Watch one story travel the line: spec drafted, gate pause for approval, build in an isolated worktree, the independent multi-lens review standing at every autonomy level, then a mechanical merge only after the full suite runs green. What ships is what was specified.

label: Three ways work flows
notes: Three flows: one attended story for judgment-heavy work; an epic batch loop-gated — the workhorse that shipped Atlas and Warden; and the unattended fleet — eight concurrent homes overnight, gates still on, review pass still standing.

label: Graduated autonomy
notes: The differentiator. L1 assistive through L5 self-governance; L3 — conditional autonomy inside context gates — is the production ceiling running here today. The supervisor watches from outside; every incident that built this slide was paid for in production: 25.8M tokens to a blind cap, three attempts to an idle strand, 13 of 31 specs to a teardown.

label: The SDLC, staffed
notes: Every pipeline stage has an owner and a skill set — today, shipped and running, and the frontier. Deployment and operations was the one orphaned stage until Steward joined the crew. Note the Build row: the marshal CLI is now in the today column.

label: The Master Pipeline relay
notes: The stations hand work along a relay: Doctor pre-flight, Herald captures the Dream, Marshal spins the factory, Atlas maps, Warden audits, Mason ships, Doctor watches, Herald proclaims. Supervised start to finish by Marshal — sequencing on verdicts it never authors; each hand-off is a durable, revision-pinned verdict artifact.

label: Act IV — The product
notes: Act IV: the product itself — the shipped CLI, the doctrine it obeys, the verb-selection guide, and the visibility layer.

label: Shipped — the marshal CLI
notes: This is no longer aspiration. Epic 1 landed 10 of 10 stories on 2026-07-31. Six commands, 785 fast tests plus 8 slow real-git tests. Every finding a coded MRS envelope; frozen exit domain; teardown refuses unmerged work; one harness seam enforced by import-linter. The cadence on the right is a real session.

label: The execution doctrine
notes: Three laws at every autonomy level: skills are the unit of execution; the harness is the unit of governance and deliberately not a skill; station verdicts stay independent. And the 2026-07-31 ruling: Marshal sequences on verdicts it never authors — gating reads durable, revision-pinned verdict artifacts. Marshal never runs the judge.

label: Which verb, when
notes: The selection guide: init for a new line, preflight before every launch, homes to audit isolation, config for policy, dev-auto for judgment-heavy stories, the loop for epics, unattended for the fleet, gate evaluate for CI, deploy and land for the last mile, teardown to retire safely.

label: Every run stays visible
notes: Visibility with consequence: sprint feeds through gates, the console regenerated from ledgers and never hand-trusted, and ten deterministic detectors patrolling the artifacts — a false green is caught by machinery, not luck. The board renders scope faithfully; it would be easier to look at if it lied.

label: Who it serves, where it runs
notes: From a solo developer to an air-gapped enterprise. The solo dev gets a second shift; the team lead a review floor that never rubber-stamps; the manager a board that cannot lie; the CTO autonomy with an audit trail. Enterprise: three pure policy layers with site config materialized at install time, internal tooling mounting through adapter profiles and the declared tool surface, local-first with no hosted control plane.

label: Proof & road
notes: Act VI: the receipts, then the map. Atlas 57 of 57; Warden 43 of 43; Marshal's own Epic 1 built by the line it now runs; 128 of 333 fleet-wide. Ahead: gates as objects, the outside supervisor, the landing paper trail, fleet status, portability proven — then the four Dreams: pr-lifecycle, durable-runs, fidelity-enforcement, one-front-door, and the installer fold.

label: Validated code, not vibes
notes: Close on the creed: the Dream deserves better than vibes. Marshal ships exactly what was specified — enforced, contained, validated. Hand off to the Guild: Atlas charts, Warden clears, Mason builds, Doctor judges, Scribe records, Steward runs the estate, Herald tells the world. Write the Dream; the factory does the rest.
